method: every read on record carries a reader field in its log line (or its run line); counted across all 16 Florida windows, the three core runs, the earlier bot log and Chicago/Illinois window one
finding: no refusal on record was taken by a plain fetch; v4’s plain-fetch re-probe has no population in Florida, Chicago or Illinois
downgrade: the Cross-Check’s second finding (“twenty-six sources and nine rows were closed by a plain fetch”) is downgraded in writing: they were closed by a browser-grade reader in the sense of a real headless browser
caveat: v4’s own definition of a browser-grade reader includes rotating proxies and rate-limit handling (section on the reader). The build’s reader is headless Chromium with a declared user agent and no proxy, so it is browser-grade in rendering and not in network identity. Whether that difference is worth a paid proxy reader is a separate decision; it is not the plain-fetch finding
